tier: USA Residential VPS Starter and Power (Windows 10 RDP)

free_tier.stated: No free tier. Starter is $34.95 monthly (4 core, 4 GB RAM, 40 GB SSD, up to 1 Gbps, Windows 10) and Power is $49.95 monthly (12 core, 12 GB RAM, 40 GB SSD). Longer terms are cheaper per month: Starter $26.25 a month on a 12-month term, Power $37.50. A 'Fresh IP' add-on that has never been used by others costs a one-time $24.95.
free_tier.notes: The longer-term monthly figures are the 12-month plan divided by 12 as the page prints them.

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented machine and its address, not stored bytes. The fresh-IP page states the address 'never changes as long you continue the service'; what happens to it at non-payment is unverified.

egress.terms: The plan lists 'Connection: up to 1 Gbps' and states no monthly byte allowance and no overage price on the pages read, so whether traffic is capped is unverified.
egress.free_allowance: unverified: no byte allowance stated on the plan pages

interface_detail: Remote Desktop (RDP) on a Windows 10 machine with full administrator access. RDP is not in the interface vocabulary, so the token is unknown. The page states no proxy endpoint.
tooling: An RDP client plus a proxy or tunnel daemon the user installs on the Windows machine. The vendor publishes no proxy endpoint and no API on the pages read.
chaining: A Worker opens an outbound connection to the machine's dedicated address and the machine makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees an address from one of the ISPs the vendor lists (Comcast Xfinity, AT&T, Century Link, Spectrum, Verizon) instead of AS13335. Locations number more than 20 across US states.

limits.value: connection up to 1 Gbps on Starter and Power; no allowance or overage price stated

limits_note: The registration class of a delivered address is the constraint the vocabulary cannot name. The vendor publishes no test address on the pages read, so no registry lookup was possible. A forum review list says the addresses carry a high fraud score and a poor ipdata reading even though the IP quality is good.
binding_note: No byte or request limit is stated, so none binds. What decides the record is the registration class of the delivered address, which is unverified because no test address is published.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the checkout fields are behind the order flow. The home page lists payment options 'Credit Cards, Paypal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, AliPay, Cash App etc.', so a card is not the only route. The kind records an email as the floor.

reliability_note: A forum list rates the vendor's address quality as good, its ipdata and fraud score as poor, its ticket response fast and its refunds quick, and advises buying a fresh address and keeping a spare route.
confidence_note: Prices, specifications and payment options are documented from the vendor's home page and fresh-IP page. The registration class, the traffic allowance and the identity fields are unverified. The forum quotes are reported, not measured.

evidence.proved: the plans state a 1 Gbps connection and no byte allowance

notes: The first-party pages sell a Windows 10 RDP machine with one dedicated address. The Starter and Power plans differ only in cores and memory. No test address is published, which is why no registry lookup is recorded here. The 12-month Power price on the page is $37.50 a month.

extras.rung_note: The product is a claim about the address class and no registry lookup is possible without a published test address.
